subject: Re: CoreWave availability floor & escalation — alignment for roadmap and approval
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: CoreWave Ops <ops@corewave.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: CoreWave availability floor & escalation — initial ask

Hi Jenna and team,

Thanks again for the call this morning. CoreWave reiterated the need for a written availability floor for the upcoming contract: a 99.99% monthly availability commitment and a p95 response floor of 150ms for the inference endpoint serving their realtime recommendations workload. They’d like this formalized in a side letter ahead of the renewal.

I attached the latest SLA draft (corewave_sla_draft_v3.pdf) and a proposed operational runbook. Before we loop legal, I need internal alignment on feasibility, expected cost uplift, and operational constraints.

Key asks:
- Can Product/SRE confirm whether p95 150ms is achievable with our current hosted model variants for that workload profile?
- If not, what are the minimum Dedicated/reserved capacity or routing policies required?
- Rough cost delta and lead time to provision (and whether quantized model variants are acceptable fallback).

Marissa — please treat this as high priority; CoreWave is strategic (Deal DW-9872). If we can agree on a constrained carveout plan, I’ll ask Legal to prepare a side letter.

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Owner, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: corewave_sla_draft_v3.pdf, operational_runbook_v1.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, CoreWave Ops <ops@corewave.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CoreWave availability floor & escalation — initial ask

Sean + Jenna,

Echoing Sean — CoreWave emphasized business impact: their SLAs with downstream partners require a firm external commitment. They’re willing to sign a multi-year commit if we can offer the availability floor but will request credits and operational commitments (runbooks, dedicated on-call).

Operational detail from CoreWave on traffic: sustained 500 rps with spikes to 900 rps during morning windows; typical request sizes are small (avg 128 tokens). They want global failover: if primary region degrades, traffic should route to a warm-secondary without degradation beyond a short failover window.

Next steps I propose:
1) Product/SRE to provide a short memo by EOD Friday with feasibility and required infrastructure changes.
2) If Dedicated is required, Ops to provide provisioning ETA and cost delta.
3) Legal to prepare side letter template once we have a technical guardrail.

Jenna — will you share any compliance artifacts Legal needs?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CoreWave availability floor & escalation — feasibility note

Team,

Quick technical readout after an initial perf-sim with CoreWave-like traces:
- Hosted: current best-case p95 for the recommended open model on gpus is ~220ms for 128-token requests at sustained 500 rps. That assumes continuous batching and our optimized kernel paths. We see tail variance during bursty spikes.
- Dedicated (reserved pool): with a dedicated 8-GPU pool (A100 class) and aggressive autoscaling thresholds, we can target p95 ~140–160ms under the described workload, but this requires:
  * Prefix/KV cache warmup (pre-warming recommended one hour prior to peak windows),
  * Dedicated routing (no cross-tenant noisy neighbors),
  * A warm-secondary region with pre-provisioned capacity and automated failover policy.

Tradeoffs and caveats:
- Cost uplift estimate: roughly 2.6x hosted baseline for the Dedicated reservation and warm-secondary. I exported the quick estimates in latency_cost_estimates.csv.
- Quantized variants reduce cost but add ~20–30ms of latency variability; not ideal for a hard 150ms p95 promise.

Suggested phased approach:
Phase A (pilot, 3 months): Dedicated pool in primary region + runbook and SLO monitoring (no formal side letter).
Phase B (commit): Side letter with availability floor, reserve capacity, warm-secondary, and quarterly operational drills.

I can draft the pilot runbook and a list of operational checks. If Product/Leadership is comfortable, we should require a dedicated funding commitment from CoreWave to cover reserved spend.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, SRE & Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: latency_cost_estimates.csv

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 14:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CoreWave availability floor & escalation — product/roadmap questions

Thanks for the analysis, Karthik. High level comments:

1) Product stance: We can support a carveout if the customer funds Dedicated capacity and agrees to a staged commitment. We’ll need a clear canary plan and a rollback policy baked into the side letter (to avoid committing our general hosted customers).

2) Roadmap ask: engineering will prioritize a "fast-failover" routing feature to automate region switchovers within the quarter, but only if we have committed customers (this would accelerate our general roadmap). That means CoreWave’s commitment will serve as a product accelerator.

3) Requirements for side letter:
- Explicit reserve size and cost responsibility (tenant pays reserved costs),
- Operational drills every quarter with both parties,
- Defined measurement methodology for p95 and permissible measurement windows,
- Fallback model variant list (primary model, quantized fallback) and expected performance delta.

Marissa/Sean — please confirm whether CoreWave is willing to sign the reserve payment and the quarterly drill cadence. Lauren — need your high-level approval to move Legal once CoreWave confirms funding.

Grace
Grace O'Connor
VP, Product Management
Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: CoreWave Ops <ops@corewave.com>, CoreWave Legal <contracts@corewave.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 16:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: CoreWave availability floor & escalation — summary & next steps

Jenna / Legal team,

Thanks for the quick conversation earlier. To summarize the internal alignment and next steps so we have a single source of truth:

Agreed technical path:
- Pilot (Phase A): Dedicated 8-GPU reservation in primary region with warm-secondary (cost estimated in latency_cost_estimates.csv). We’ll run a 6-week pilot window focused on pre-warm ops and tracelogging.
- Commit (Phase B): If pilot meets the measurement methodology, Redwood will sign a side letter with 99.99% monthly availability and a p95 measurement methodology for the specific endpoint. The tenant (CoreWave) will pay reserved capacity costs.

Action items and owners:
- Karthik: Provide provisioning ETA and a draft pilot runbook by Tue, 15 Dec. (attachment: operational_runbook_v1.xlsx)
- Marissa: Confirm commercial terms with CoreWave (reserve payment and drill cadence) by Wed, 16 Dec.
- Grace / Lauren: If commercial terms confirmed, Legal to start side letter drafting (Lauren to approve go-ahead).
- Sean: Coordinate final DocuSign routing once Legal issues a draft.

Jenna — can you confirm reserve funding and whether CoreWave expects credits if SLOs are missed? If they do, please indicate the expected credit model so Legal can draft appropriately.

Thanks all — we’ll treat this as a high-priority cross-functional run.

Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Owner, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
